signals.reasoning: As a defensive investor, I must firmly reject GE at its present valuation. The enterprise fails our basic financial strength test with a current ratio of just 0.98—well below the conservative 1.5 minimum—while book value per share has steadily eroded from $30.94 in 2022 to $16.89 today. Furthermore, paying a P/E multiple of nearly 38 capitalizes unproven future growth rather than established value

GE has refocused into a high-quality enterprise, driving returns on equity up to 52% alongside strong free cash flow of $7.73 per share. However, book value per share has shrunk significantly over the past four years, and top-line growth has slowed down to 4%. At nearly 38 times earnings, the market is charging an exorbitant price for this turnaround, leaving us without the proper margin of safety

Paying nearly 38 times earnings for a business growing top-line revenues at a meager 4% is financial insanity. Book value per share has steadily eroded from $30.94 down to $16.89 while debt levels have crept up and current liquidity has dropped below 1.0. A great business compounds intrinsic value over time; this one is melting down its equity base while Mr. Market demands a heroic price.
